newsitem.title: USA: Baby whale rescued off California dies.
newsitem.headline: Baby whale rescued off California dies.

text.p: A 3-month-old gray whale calf rescued from shallow water off the central California coast last week died Monday at San Diego's Sea World from an infection, officials said.

The 16-foot (5 meter) 2,900-pound (1315-kg) calf was on antibiotics and being fed a special formula and was initially thought to be recovering. But over the weekend it grew sluggish and unresponsive to the attendants who were caring for it in a closed-in isolation pool, a spokesman said.

"There simply wasn't anything else we could do to save her. We knew the prognosis was not good when we first examined her, but we wanted to try everything we could to bring her back to health," said Sea World veterinarian Dr Tom Reidarson.
Sea World officials said the calf was severely dehydrated and emaciated. It was transported to Sea World last Friday. Officials speculated the calf was abandoned by its mother, who may have been ill.
Another calf, rescued off Los Angeles in January, has responded well to treatment, Reidarson said. The whale, named J.J., will be reintroduced to the ocean late this year or early next year.
The gray whales are currently migrating from Mexico's Baja peninsula to the wtaers off the Pacific Northwest region.
